# Education in Sweden
Education in Sweden is structured into distinct levels, beginning with preschool (förskola) for children aged 1–6, followed by a mandatory nine-year comprehensive school (grundskola) covering ages 6–16. The compulsory school is divided into lower, middle, and upper stages, with students taking a broad curriculum of 16 core subjects. Grading starts in year 6 using a scale from A to F. Upper secondary education (gymnasieskola), though elective, sees near-universal enrollment and is divided into 18 national programmes—preparatory and vocational—all of which provide basic qualification for university entry. Students’ admission to gymnasium is based on their elementary school grades, and eligibility criteria involve passing certain core subjects.
Higher education in Sweden adheres to the Bologna Process, offering three cycles: bachelor's (three years), master's (one or two years), and doctoral programs (two or four years). Universities and university colleges provide both general academic and professional degrees. Admission requires proficiency in Swedish and English, and the Swedish Scholastic Aptitude Test (Högskoleprovet) may be required. Students receive financial support via loans and grants. Independent (friskolor) schools, publicly funded but privately managed, have grown since the 1992 reform, now educating a significant share of students. While Sweden has demonstrated strong early childhood provision and near-total participation at all levels, recent years have seen concerns over declining educational standards and increased grade inflation, especially among independent schools.
